title: Transport of the single-refinement projection square to field coefficients
statement: Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. The schemes are finite-type schemes over its field, with separated finite-type morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Compactifications and proper refinements are those of [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $S$ be the normalized six-functor operation datum, with $\ell$ invertible in the base field. At both the rational stage $E$ and the common-stage $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], the predicate $\mathrm{refinementLaw}$ of [def-sf-projection-single-refinement-law] holds for all bounded constructible inputs ($P=\mathrm{True}$), using each stage's recorded tensor, pullback, projection and compactification comparison. This asserts the local square for one proper refinement only; it does not assert comparison independence for arbitrary pairs.

source.place: Compactification-independence sentence: compatibility of refinement comparisons with the counits and j_!, together with naturality.

proof.text: Promote integralRefinementProjection to the integral comparison equation for any two compactifications: choose a common refinement, cancel its first comparison square, compose with its second square, and use comparison_trans. The two identity-square constructions identitySquare and compactSupportProjectionSquare are definitionally equal. Combine this comparison equation with integralStageProjection_structuralIdentities to obtain CompactSupportProjectionCoherence for the integral stage. The structural-identities proof plan uses only integral refinement squares for its proper coincidence clause.

Apply compactSupportProjectionCoherence_rational to this integral coherence. For every finite coefficient field in the closure, construct its operation datum using finiteLevels 0 of coefficientIntegralNormalization, the recorded higher coefficient stage, and the same closure/coherence data. Repeat the integral coherence construction and rational transport at that field.

Apply compactSupportProjectionCoherence_common to the family of rational coherence results. For each of the two requested refinement laws, take the compactification field of the corresponding coherence result, reverse the equality, and specialize it to the supplied pair of compactifications. No use of the supplied refinement is needed because the comparison equation now holds for every pair.

theorem fieldRefinementProjection
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (C : D.CoefficientDatum)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E] (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (S : SixFunctorOperationDatum D C E n hn) (hl : IsUnit (C.l : D.k)) :
    refinementLaw S.higher.rational S.higher.rationalTensor S.higher.rationalExchange
      (fun _ _ ↦ True) ∧
    refinementLaw S.closure.commonStage S.closure.commonStageTensor S.closure.commonStageExchange
      (fun _ _ ↦ True)
